chapter: Leading a band: Beverly Gardens to Honeysuckle Inn
title: Beverly Gardens gambling raid and the 25 Cent Club opening
summary: After Crum left, Frank and Bill Padron formed a band with Eddie Miller and Armand Hug at Beverly Gardens, which was raided, then opened the 25 Cent Club.

bands.name: Bill Padron and Frank Netto's band

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then after Crum left, what happened? How did that happen? Well, after Crum left,

the job expired and we decided that we could build Padron and myself. That's when we got Eddie Miller and Almond Hub and we started off with Johnny LaPorte on the drums. And I went up, Bill and I went over to Suburban Gardens that time. No, no, no, it wasn't Suburban, no, I'm sorry, it wasn't Suburban Gardens. It was Beverly Gardens. That was when the guy, the old man that was running the gambling house up there, Beverly Garden, do you remember? What the hell his name was? Beverly Gardens, that was when that was where Primer was? I'm talking about Beverly Gardens on Metry Road. I'm talking about when Primer bought it after that.

I don't know, did they change its name to the Avalon after that? Well, it used to be Beverly Gardens when I worked up there. Beverly Gardens and they changed it. You went up the hill and your gardens around there and it was a gambling giant. Well, that's where we went to work in there.
There was Victory Gardens, there was a Victory Inn. There was Victory Inn. There was a
Another place. There was a Metry Inn and Beverly Gardens. That's the three
gambling joints out there. Well, Beverly Gardens wasn't, when Primer owned it, it was not a gambling

joint. Huh? No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. You didn't want to put them out of business then, but we worked up there until the night they raided it. I was on the bandstand when they raided it. They put a sticker on a little button and Getz, Tommy Getz was the guy that ran the place. He was the gambler. And he told me, he says, if you see me stick my finger in my ear like this, press this button over there to let them know in the gambling room that the police were here. So I told him, all right, it was laying right alongside of me. I was standing in the corner and it was hung right there. And so the night that they did raid the place, we didn't do much business. They didn't want us to do any business. Bring the people in there. If they decide to dance, stop playing music. They wanted to get in there and gamble. But Alfred was good outside of Johnny Lepore. Johnny, I mean, that's when I got, uh, we got, uh, we got Von Gammon in there then. But, uh, the night that the raid came in, the first guy I saw came right to the bandstand and says, don't you dare to put your hand on out of it. He says, I'll throw you in jail. And believe me, I didn't touch it. So they caught them all, all the loaded dice and everything else. So it went on for a few weeks after that. And Kefaubber, Kefaubber was down here, when Eddie

Hebert was, uh, some dinner for Eddie Hebert, which I had the music for. And Kefaubber came down here, was when, Kefaubber was the one that put all of these guys out of business. Yeah. Yeah. And, uh, they had a special, uh, before the dinner, they had the VIP room, cocktails before the dinner. And I went over there and Eddie, who had autographed my album. And, uh, Leon was just born. This was in 1952, 51. And, uh, I got Mr. Kefaubber to, uh, uh, to, uh, autograph my program, too. He was the principal speaker. So, uh, he, he wrote on, he said, thanks for your wonderful music. It's a pleasure to hear you. So I, after I looked at what he wrote, I said, Mr. Kefaubber, I said, I can get you on perjury. I said, you haven't even seen, you haven't even heard my music yet. Thanks for your wonderful music. He said, well, don't hold out against me. He said, I'll listen to it after a while. And we go inside. But, uh, he was, he was the one that wrote Sheriff Clancy. That's when Clancy was the, was the sheriff up there.

Yeah, but you're talking about several years after. Yeah, this is after. This is long before that. Well, because when, uh, Huey Long was a guard, it shut, uh, shut Tommy Gets down. Yeah, he shut him down. So, uh, then we left there. We stayed there a few weeks after that. And, uh, we let, uh, then we let, uh, Johnny Laporte go because, I don't think Johnny played well enough. Bill didn't like him and Eddie Miller didn't like, care for him that much either. So then we went out. Our next job was the Hunnis, was, uh, the 25 Cent Club. We went out there. And, uh, because Honeysuckle Inn and the Petting them. Well you went the Honeysuckle Inn or the 25 Cent Club? No, we went the 25 Cent Club first. We opened them up. Because the Honeysuckle Inn was in business a long long time. But then, uh, they remodeled them. Do you remember them? From the time you went in there and you had a pea and a barrel? And then they put them toilets in them. But, uh, them the Honeysuckle Inn They opened up the place and that was the... we stayed in there for a couple of years. Well, was it this the same time when... Then we left there and went up to the hospital.
